note:
Structuring a recipe as Before You Start ➔ Ingredients ➔ Instructions creates a logical timeline for the cook.
Here is why this specific order works so well:
• Before You Start (The "Mindset"): This alerts the cook to things they need to do hours or minutes before cooking (e.g., marinating, bringing butter to room temperature, or preheating the oven). It prevents the frustrating realization of reading step 4 of a recipe only to find out the meat needed to marinate overnight.
• Ingredients (The "Shopping & Gathering"): This lists everything the cook needs to pull out of the pantry and fridge. Because the "Before You Start" section already addressed temperatures or specific prep rules, the cook knows exactly how to handle these items.
• Instructions (The "Execution"): This is the step-by-step roadmap. Because the first two sections set the stage, the instructions can focus purely on active cooking without clunky disruptions.
